testo_originale: Article 2 This Regulation shall enter into force on the 20th day following its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union .

testo_originale: 4. Paragraphs 1, 2 and 3 shall be without prejudice to:

testo_originale: 5. Any restriction of the rights and obligations, referred to in paragraph 2, shall be necessary and proportionate taking into account the risks to the rights and freedoms of data subjects.
descrizione_funzionale: Substantive proportionality clause that conditions any limitation on the earlier-listed rights and duties, requiring the measure to be justified by necessity and calibrated to the relevant risks. testo_originale: Article 3 Provision of information to data subjects
descrizione_funzionale: Introductory operative provision identifying the subject-matter of the following rules and signalling that the act will regulate how information is to be given in this specific context. It sits at a relatively high structural level within the decision, but remains more concrete than a general principle because it frames a distinct operational area rather than setting a detailed procedure itself.

testo_originale: 1. The Commission shall publish on its website data protection notices that inform all data subjects of its activities involving processing of their personal data for the purposes of analyses and procedures with regard to the screening of foreign direct investments or the cooperation mechanism under Regulation (EU) 2019/452. Where it is possible to do so without jeopardising the functioning of the cooperation mechanism, the Commission shall ensure that the data subjects are informed individually in an appropriate format.
descrizione_funzionale: Operational transparency rule requiring the Commission to make public notices and, where feasible, provide individual notice to affected persons about its processing activities, thereby implementing the broader duty to inform in a concrete communicative form. It sits at a fairly specific level: not a general principle, but a practical rule governing how information must be delivered in this particular administrative context, with an exception calibrated to preserve the effective functioning of the underlying mechanism.

testo_originale: 2. Where the Commission restricts, wholly or partly, the provision of information to data subjects whose data are processed for the purposes of analyses and procedures with regard to the screening of foreign direct investments or the cooperation mechanism under Regulation (EU) 2019/452, it shall record and register the reasons for the restriction in accordance with Article 6 of this Decision.
descrizione_funzionale: Record-keeping clause requiring the Commission to document and register the reasons whenever it limits information to affected individuals, thereby operationalising accountability and traceability for a restrictive measure. It sits at a fairly specific, implementation-oriented level: it does not create the restriction itself, but prescribes the internal evidentiary and procedural step that must accompany that restriction in a defined context.

testo_originale: Article 4 Right of access by data subject, right of erasure and right to restriction of processing
descrizione_funzionale: Substantive rights clause identifying three specific entitlements that are subject to the internal regime and signalling the point at which those rights may be exercised or limited within the procedure. It operates at an operational level: more specific than the general framework, but still setting a core rule for a defined category of cases rather than a mere technical detail.

testo_originale: 1. Where the Commission restricts, wholly or partly, the right of access to personal data by data subjects, the right of erasure, or the right to restriction of processing, as referred to respectively in Articles 17, 19 and 20 of Regulation (EU) 2018/1725, it shall inform the data subject concerned, in its reply to the request for access, erasure or restriction of processing:
descrizione_funzionale: Operative procedural rule that triggers a notification duty whenever the Commission relies on a partial or total restriction of specified individual rights, linking that restriction to the response given on the underlying request. It sits at a fairly specific, implementation-oriented level: it does not create the restriction itself, but regulates how that restriction must be communicated in a concrete case.

testo_originale: (a) of the restriction applied and of the principal reasons thereof; and
descrizione_funzionale: Operative disclosure requirement specifying one element of the notice that must be given when a right is curtailed, namely the fact of the restriction and the main reasons for it. testo_originale: (b) of the possibility of lodging a complaint with the European Data Protection Supervisor or of seeking a judicial remedy in the Court of Justice of the European Union.
descrizione_funzionale: Informational clause requiring that the person be told about available avenues for challenging the measure, thereby safeguarding procedural accountability and access to oversight. testo_originale: 2. The provision of information concerning the reasons for the restriction referred to in paragraph 1 may be deferred, omitted or denied for as long as it would undermine the purpose of the restriction.
descrizione_funzionale: Exception clause qualifying the information duty by allowing disclosure of the reasons for a restriction to be postponed, withheld, or refused where disclosure would defeat the restriction’s purpose. It operates at a fairly specific, operational level, supplying a narrow safeguard that calibrates how the general duty to inform is applied in concrete cases.

testo_originale: 3. The Commission shall record and register the reasons for the restriction in accordance with Article
descrizione_funzionale: Record-keeping obligation requiring the institution to document and register the grounds justifying the limitation, thereby creating an internal accountability and traceability duty linked to the use of the restriction power. It is a narrow operational rule, highly specific in its application and serving as an implementation detail within a broader procedural framework.

testo_originale: 4. Where the right of access is wholly or partly restricted, the data subject may exercise his or her right of access through the intermediary of the European Data Protection Supervisor, in accordance with Article 25(6), (7) and (8) of Regulation (EU) 2018/1725.
descrizione_funzionale: Procedural safeguard clause creating an alternative channel for exercising access rights when direct access has been restricted, and cross-referencing the applicable supervisory procedure in another instrument. It operates at a fairly specific, operational level: not a general principle, but a targeted mechanism that activates only in the restricted-access scenario and only for the particular right concerned.

testo_originale: Article 5 Communication of personal data breaches to data subjects Where the Commission restricts the communication of a personal data breach to the data subject, as referred to in Article 35 of Regulation (EU) 2018/1725, it shall record and register the reasons for the restriction in accordance with Article 6 of this Decision.
descrizione_funzionale: Record-keeping obligation that operationalises a prior restriction by requiring the Commission to document and register the reasons whenever it withholds communication of a breach to the individual concerned. It is a narrow implementing rule at a low level of abstraction, triggered only in the specific case where the restriction is applied and serving to support traceability and accountability rather than setting the restriction itself.

testo_originale: Article 6 Recording and registering of restrictions
descrizione_funzionale: Operative rule requiring that any restriction adopted under the framework be formally recorded and entered in a register, thereby creating an internal accountability and traceability mechanism for exceptional measures. It sits at a practical, implementation-focused level: not a broad principle, but a procedural safeguard that applies whenever such a restriction is imposed.

testo_originale: 1. The Commission shall record the reasons for any restriction applied pursuant to this Decision, including an assessment of the necessity and proportionality of the restriction, taking into account the relevant elements set out in Article 25(2) of Regulation (EU) 2018/1725.
descrizione_funzionale: Record-keeping and justification clause that obliges the institution to document why a restriction is imposed and to assess its necessity and proportionality, while also tying that assessment to an external reference norm. It operates at an operational level: not a general principle, but a concrete procedural safeguard that applies whenever such a restriction is used.

testo_originale: 2. The record shall state how the exercise of a right by the relevant data subject would jeopardise the purpose of the Commission’s analyses and procedures with regard to the screening of foreign direct investments or the cooperation mechanism under Regulation (EU) 2019/452, or of restrictions applied pursuant to Article 2(2) or (3) of this Decision, or would adversely affect the rights and freedoms of other data subjects.
descrizione_funzionale: Operational rule requiring the record to document the concrete reasons why exercising a right would undermine the effectiveness of the Commission’s analyses and procedures or harm the rights and freedoms of others. It sits at a fairly technical, case-specific level, implementing the broader restriction regime by prescribing the evidentiary content that must be captured whenever such a limitation is applied.

testo_originale: 3. The record and, where applicable, the documents containing underlying factual and legal elements shall be registered. They shall be made available to the European Data Protection Supervisor on request.
descrizione_funzionale: Operational record-keeping rule that requires the relevant material to be formally registered and, on request, disclosed to the supervisory authority, thereby ensuring traceability and oversight. It sits at a fairly specific, implementation-focused level, translating a broader accountability requirement into a concrete administrative duty for a defined category of records and documents.

testo_originale: Article 7 Duration of restrictions
descrizione_funzionale: Provision fixing the temporal scope of the restrictive measure by stating how long it may remain in force and when it must cease to apply. It operates at a fairly specific, implementation-oriented level: it does not create the restriction itself, but regulates the lifespan of an already authorised exception within the framework.

testo_originale: 1. The restrictions referred to in Articles 3, 4 and 5 shall continue to apply as long as the reasons justifying them remain applicable.
descrizione_funzionale: Continuity clause maintaining the effect of previously imposed restrictions for the duration of the underlying justification, thereby linking the persistence of the measure to an ongoing factual basis. It operates at a specific operational level, not creating a new power or rule but setting the temporal condition under which an existing limitation remains in force.

testo_originale: 2. Where the reasons for a restriction referred to in Article 3 or 5 no longer apply, the Commission shall lift the restriction and provide the principal reasons for the restriction to the data subject. At the same time, the Commission shall inform the data subject of the possibility of lodging a complaint with the European Data Protection Supervisor at any time or of seeking a judicial remedy in the Court of Justice of the European Union.
descrizione_funzionale: Operative safeguard clause that ends a restriction once its justification has fallen away and requires the Commission to disclose the main reasons, while also informing the person concerned of available avenues of redress. It sits at a fairly specific, implementation-focused level: it does not set the grounds for restricting rights, but regulates the follow-up duties that arise when those grounds cease to exist.

testo_originale: 3. The Commission shall review the application of the restrictions referred to in Articles 3 and 5 one year after adoption and at the closure of the relevant Commission analyses and procedures carried out with regard to the screening of foreign direct investments or the cooperation mechanism under Regulation (EU) 2019/452. Thereafter, the Commission shall monitor the need to maintain any restriction. The review shall include an assessment of the necessity and proportionality of the restriction, taking into account the relevant elements set out in Article 25(2) of Regulation (EU) 2018/1725.
descrizione_funzionale: Post-adoption review clause imposing a continuing supervisory duty on the Commission to reassess whether the restrictions remain justified, including a necessity-and-proportionality check and reference to the relevant criteria in the general data-protection framework. It operates at an intermediate, operational level: not a broad principle, but a procedural control mechanism that governs how an already-authorised restriction must be periodically revalidated and maintained.

testo_originale: Article 8 Review by the Data Protection Officer of the Commission 1. The Data Protection Officer of the Commission shall be informed, without undue delay, whenever data subjects’ rights are restricted in accordance with this Decision. Upon request, the Data Protection Officer shall be provided with access to the record and any documents containing underlying factual and legal elements. 2. The Data Protection Officer may request a review of the restriction. The Data Protection Officer shall be informed about the outcome of the requested review. 3. The Commission shall document the involvement of the Data Protection Officer in each case where the application of rights and obligations referred to in Article 2(2) is restricted.
descrizione_funzionale: Procedural oversight clause assigning the internal data protection officer a review and information role whenever rights are restricted, including access to the relevant record and the ability to trigger a reassessment. It operates at an intermediate, institutional level: not a general principle, but a supervisory mechanism that structures how the restriction decision is checked and documented in individual cases.

testo_originale: Article 9 Entry into force This Decision shall enter into force on the third day following that of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union.
descrizione_funzionale: Commencement clause determining when the decision becomes legally operative by tying its effect to publication and a short waiting period. It is highly specific and purely procedural, applying across the whole instrument without adding any substantive rule, only fixing the moment from which the framework starts to bind.

testo_originale: Article 1 Annex II to Implementing Regulation (EU) 2023/1441 is corrected as follows: (1) (does not concern the English language) ; (2) in Table 1, note (***) is replaced by the following: ‘(***) Use the following ranges: “ EUR 4-50 million ”, “ EUR > 50-100 million ”, “ EUR > 100-500 million ”, “ EUR > 500-1 000 million ”, “ more than EUR 1 000 million ”.’

descrizione_funzionale: Introductory scope clause that identifies the regulatory field and specifies the concrete procedural matters covered, while cross-referencing the enabling provision that authorises these detailed arrangements. testo_originale: Article 2 Definitions For the purposes of this Regulation, the following definitions shall apply: (1) ‘Notifying parties’ for the purpose of notifications of concentrations means persons or undertakings required to submit a notification pursuant to Article 21(3) of Regulation (EU) 2022/2560. (2) ‘Other persons involved’ for the purpose of notifications of concentrations mean persons involved in the proposed concentration other than the notifying parties, such as the seller and the undertaking or part of the undertaking that is the target of the concentration. (3) ‘Notifying parties’ for the purpose of notifications and declarations regarding foreign financial contributions in public procurement’ means all economic operators, groups of economic operators, main subcontractors and main suppliers covered by the notification obligation in accordance with Article 29(5) of Regulation (EU) 2022/2560. (4) ‘Working days’ means all days other than Saturdays, Sundays, and Commission holidays as published in the Official Journal of the European Union .
descrizione_funzionale: Definitional provision that fixes the meaning of key terms and cross-references the substantive obligations in the parent act, thereby determining who is captured by the procedural duties and how time is counted. It operates at a mid-level of abstraction: not a broad policy statement, but a technical interpretive rule that structures the application of the whole procedure in specific cases.

testo_originale: Article 3 Persons entitled to submit notifications and declarations
descrizione_funzionale: Operative provision identifying who may lawfully initiate the notification or declaration process, thereby allocating standing and channeling access to the procedure. It sits at a practical, mid-level of abstraction: more specific than a general organising principle, but still framing the procedural gateway rather than regulating a single technical step.

testo_originale: 1. Notifications of concentrations pursuant to Article 21 of Regulation (EU) 2022/2560 shall be submitted by the notifying parties as referred in Article 2, point (1). Each notifying party shall be responsible for the correctness of the information provided by it.
descrizione_funzionale: Operative filing rule that specifies who must submit the notification in concentration cases and allocates responsibility for the accuracy of the information provided. It sits at a fairly technical, application-level position in the framework, implementing a procedural requirement for a defined category of proceedings rather than laying down a general principle.

testo_originale: 2. Notifications and declarations in public procurement procedures shall be submitted to the contracting authority or contracting entity by the economic operator, or, in the case of groups of economic operators, main subcontractors and main suppliers, the main contractor or main concessionaire, referred to in Article 29(6) of Regulation (EU) 2022/2560 on its behalf and on behalf of any and all notifying parties as referred to in Article 2, point (3). Each notifying party shall only be responsible for the correctness of information linked to the foreign financial contributions that have been granted to it.
descrizione_funzionale: Operative allocation rule specifying who must file the required notifications and declarations, and how responsibility for the accuracy of the information is distributed among the parties involved. It sits at a fairly technical, implementation-focused level, translating a broader procedural obligation into a precise rule for a particular type of procurement situation.

testo_originale: 3. Where notifications or declarations are signed by authorised external representatives of persons or of undertakings, such representatives shall produce written proof that they are authorised to act.
descrizione_funzionale: Operative evidentiary rule requiring an authorised external representative to substantiate, in writing, their mandate when signing a notification or declaration. It sits at a fairly specific, implementation-focused level, adding a procedural safeguard that applies only in the defined representation scenario rather than laying down a general framework principle.

testo_originale: Article 4 Prior notification of concentrations
descrizione_funzionale: Heading provision that identifies and delimits a specific procedural chapter, signalling that the following rules govern the advance filing stage for a particular category of transactions. It operates at a fairly concrete, organising level: not a substantive rule itself, but a structural entry point that frames a distinct procedural sequence within the wider regime.

testo_originale: 1. Notifications of concentrations pursuant to Article 21 of Regulation (EU) 2022/2560 shall be submitted using the form for notifying concentrations set out in Annex I. Joint notifications pursuant to Article 21(3) of Regulation (EU) 2022/2560 shall be submitted on a single form.
descrizione_funzionale: Procedural rule prescribing the mandatory filing format for a particular category of notifications, and specifying that a joint filing must be made on one common form. It operates at a fairly technical, implementation-focused level, translating a higher-order procedural requirement into a concrete submission rule for a defined type of case.

testo_originale: 2. The form for notifying concentrations and all relevant supporting documents shall be submitted to the Commission in accordance with Article
descrizione_funzionale: Procedural filing rule requiring that the notification form and all supporting materials be lodged with the Commission in the manner laid down by a cross-referenced provision, thereby operationalising the initiation of the relevant proceeding. It sits at a fairly specific, implementation-focused level, translating a higher-order procedural framework into a concrete submission requirement for a defined category of cases.

testo_originale: 3. Notifications shall be submitted in one of the official languages of the Union. testo_originale: 4. The Commission may, upon written request, dispense a requesting notifying party with the obligation to provide any information in the notification form set out in Annex I, including documents, or with any other requirement in the notification form related to this information.
descrizione_funzionale: Discretionary waiver clause conferring on the Commission the power to relieve a notifying party, on written request, from specified disclosure obligations in the notification form, including supporting documents and related requirements. testo_originale: 5. The Commission shall without delay acknowledge in writing to the notifying parties receipt of the notification and of any reply to a letter sent by the Commission pursuant to Article 6(2) and (3).
descrizione_funzionale: Procedural obligation requiring the authority to issue prompt written acknowledgment upon receiving a notification or a reply, thereby structuring the handling of incoming submissions and ensuring formal traceability. It is a narrow operational rule, highly specific to one step in the proceedings and implementing a small administrative detail rather than laying down any broad substantive principle.

testo_originale: Article 5 Notifications and declarations of foreign financial contributions in the context of public procurement procedures
descrizione_funzionale: Operative heading that identifies the procedural stage in which parties must submit information about external financial support within procurement proceedings, thereby anchoring the ensuing obligations and triggering the relevant reporting mechanism. It sits at an intermediate level of abstraction: more specific than a general principle, but still framing a whole category of cases rather than a single technical detail.

testo_originale: 1. Notifications of foreign financial contributions in the context of public procurement procedures shall be submitted using the form set out in Annex II on one form containing information regarding all of the notifying parties related to one tender or request to participate, to the contracting authority or contracting entity in charge of the relevant public procurement procedure in line with Article 29(1) of Regulation (EU) 2022/2560.
descrizione_funzionale: Operational filing rule that prescribes the mandatory format and channel for submitting a notification in a specific procedural setting, while also cross-referencing the higher-ranking provision that identifies the competent recipient. It sits at a fairly technical level, implementing a narrow administrative detail that governs how one category of submission must be made rather than setting any broader substantive standard.

testo_originale: 2. Where, in public procurement procedures meeting the thresholds in Articles 28(1)(a) and 28(2) of Regulation (EU) 2022/2560, no notifiable foreign financial contributions in the last 3 years have been granted by a third country to the notifying parties, those parties must submit, instead of a notification, a declaration. The declaration must be submitted in the manner prescribed by heading 7 of the Introduction and Section 7 of Annex II on one form, to the contracting authority or contracting entity in charge of the relevant public procurement procedure. In accordance with Articles 4(3) and 29(1) of Regulation (EU) 2022/2560, foreign financial contributions the total amount of which per third country is lower than the amount of de minimis aid as defined in Article 3(2), first subparagraph, of Regulation (EU) No 1407/2013 over the consecutive period of three years preceding the declaration do not have to be reported in the declaration.
descrizione_funzionale: Operative rule replacing the ordinary notification duty with a simplified declaration when a defined factual condition is met, and simultaneously setting the content, form, and recipient of that declaration while carving out a reporting exemption for contributions below a specified quantitative floor. It sits at a highly technical, implementation-focused level, translating a higher-order reporting regime into a narrow procedural mechanism for a particular class of cases.

testo_originale: 3. The notification, including all relevant supporting documents, or the declaration shall be transferred by the contracting authority or contracting entity to the Commission in accordance with Article
descrizione_funzionale: Operational transfer rule assigning the contracting authority or entity the duty to forward the notification or declaration, together with supporting material, to the Commission by reference to the applicable procedural provision. It sits at a fairly specific, implementation-oriented level: not a general principle, but a narrow logistical step that activates within a defined proceeding and channels information to the competent institution.

testo_originale: 4. Notifications and declarations shall be submitted to the contracting authority or contracting entity in one of the official languages of the Union. Unless the Commission and the notifying parties agree otherwise, the language of the notification or declaration shall also be the language of the proceeding, as well as that of any subsequent administrative proceedings before the Commission under Regulation (EU) 2022/2560 relating to the same public procurement procedure.Supporting documents shall be submitted in their original language. descrizione_funzionale: Procedural rule governing the language regime for submissions and supporting materials, including the default language of the proceedings and the need for translations where necessary. It operates at an operational, highly specific level, implementing a narrow administrative detail that regulates how parties must communicate within a particular type of proceeding.

testo_originale: 5. The Commission may, upon written request by the notifying parties, and informing the contracting authority or contracting entity in charge of the public procurement procedure, dispense a requesting notifying party with the obligation to provide any information in the notification form set out in Annex II, including documents, or with any other requirement in the notification form related to that information.
descrizione_funzionale: Discretionary exemption clause empowering the Commission to relieve a notifying party, on written request and with notice to the relevant procurement authority, from specified disclosure obligations in the notification form. It operates at a fairly granular, procedural level: a targeted exception to the general information-submission requirements, applicable only in the particular case where the Commission chooses to waive them.

testo_originale: 6. The Commission shall without delay acknowledge the receipt of the notification or declaration and of any reply to a letter sent by the Commission pursuant to Article 7(1) and (3), in writing to the contracting authority or contracting entity in charge of the public procurement procedure, with a copy of the acknowledgment sent to the notifying parties or their authorised external representatives.
descrizione_funzionale: Procedural obligation requiring the Commission to promptly confirm receipt of a filing or response and to communicate that confirmation to the authority running the procedure, while also copying the relevant parties or their representatives. This is a narrow operational rule, highly specific in application, that implements the broader procedural framework by regulating a single step in the handling of submissions.

testo_originale: Article 6 Effective date of notification in concentrations
descrizione_funzionale: Operative rule fixing when a notification is deemed effective in concentration cases, thereby determining the point from which procedural consequences begin to run. It sits at a fairly specific, technical level, implementing a narrow timing mechanism within the broader procedural framework rather than laying down a general principle.

testo_originale: 1. Pursuant to Article 24(1) of Regulation (EU) 2022/2560, the effective date of a notification shall be the date on which the Commission receives a complete notification.
descrizione_funzionale: This provision fixes the legal trigger point for a notification by tying its effectiveness to the moment the Commission receives a complete filing, thereby determining when procedural consequences begin to run. It is a highly specific operational rule, implementing a narrow timing mechanism within the broader procedural framework rather than laying down any general principle.

testo_originale: 2. Where the Commission finds that the information, including documents, contained in the notification is incomplete, the Commission shall inform the notifying parties or their authorised external representatives in writing without delay. In such cases, the notification shall become effective on the date on which the complete information is received by the Commission.
descrizione_funzionale: Operative procedural rule governing the handling of an incomplete filing: it obliges the authority to notify the parties in writing without delay and links legal effectiveness to the later receipt of complete information. testo_originale: Article 26 Transmission and signature of documents in the context of public procurement procedures (notifications and ex officio)
descrizione_funzionale: Operational provision governing how documents are formally transmitted and authenticated within a defined category of proceedings, ensuring that notifications and self-initiated cases follow a controlled documentary channel. descrizione_funzionale: Operational rule prescribing the channel for exchanging documents in a specific procedural setting, while allowing a limited exception where the authority expressly permits alternative methods. testo_originale: 2. testo_originale: 4. When signing the documents and transmitting them to the Commission in the context of public procurement procedures, Article 25(4) and (5) shall apply by analogy.

testo_originale: Article 27 Entry into force This Regulation shall enter into force on the day following that of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union .
descrizione_funzionale: Commencement clause determining the moment from which the act becomes legally operative, thereby activating all of its procedural and institutional effects. testo_originale: Article 1 Annex I to Regulation (EC) No 184/2005 is amended as set out in the Annex to this Regulation.

testo_originale: Article 2 This Regulation shall enter into force on the twentieth day following that of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union . descrizione_funzionale: Commencement and application clause that fixes when the act becomes legally operative and when its practical effects begin for a defined category of transmissions, thereby triggering the temporal reach of the amendment. testo_originale: Article 1 Member States shall supply on an annual basis a quality report drawn up in accordance with the rules laid down in the Annex.

testo_originale: Article 3 This Regulation shall enter into force on the 20th day following its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union .
descrizione_funzionale: Commencement clause determining when the act becomes legally operative by fixing the date on which its binding effects begin. It is a universal, terminal rule with a very high degree of abstraction, applying to the entire instrument without adding any substantive content.

testo_originale: Article 1 The Annex to Regulation (EU) 2019/452 is replaced by the text in the Annex to this Regulation.
descrizione_funzionale: Operative amendment clause that substitutes the existing annex with a new text, thereby updating the content of the parent act without creating a standalone substantive rule. testo_originale: Article 2 This Regulation shall enter into force on the twentieth day following that of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union .
descrizione_funzionale: Commencement clause fixing the moment from which the amending act becomes legally operative, thereby triggering its binding effects after publication. It is a highly specific, purely procedural rule that applies universally to the instrument as a whole without adding any substantive content.

testo_originale: Article 1 Subject matter and scope
descrizione_funzionale: Introductory provision that delineates the act’s subject matter and the outer boundaries of its application, thereby organising the reach of the whole framework. It operates at a high level of abstraction, because it does not yet prescribe concrete procedures or outcomes but instead frames what the regulation is meant to cover and where it applies.

testo_originale: 1. This Regulation establishes a framework for the screening by Member States of foreign direct investments into the Union on the grounds of security or public order and for a mechanism for cooperation between Member States, and between Member States and the Commission, with regard to foreign direct investments likely to affect security or public order. It includes the possibility for the Commission to issue opinions on such investments.
descrizione_funzionale: Foundational operative clause that defines the regulation’s core architecture by creating the screening framework, setting the cooperation mechanism, and recognising an advisory role for the Commission. It sits at a high level of abstraction, because it frames the overall system and its institutional relationships rather than laying down detailed conditions or procedures for individual cases.

testo_originale: 2. This Regulation is without prejudice to each Member State having sole responsibility for its national security, as provided for in Article 4(2) TEU, and to the right of each Member State to protect its essential security interests in accordance with Article 346 TFEU.
descrizione_funzionale: This clause preserves and cross-refers to higher-ranking Treaty-based competences, carving out that the Regulation does not displace Member States’ retained authority in matters of security and essential interests. It operates at a very high level of abstraction, functioning as a constitutional-style limitation on the reach of the instrument rather than as a technical rule for individual cases.

testo_originale: 3. Nothing in this Regulation shall limit the right of each Member State to decide whether or not to screen a particular foreign direct investment within the framework of this Regulation.
descrizione_funzionale: Preservative clause safeguarding national discretion by clarifying that the framework does not oblige a Member State to examine every incoming investment, but leaves the initial choice to screen or not to screen to each state. It operates at a high structural level: not a technical rule, but a boundary-setting norm that allocates room for domestic decision-making within the overall regime.

testo_originale: Article 2 Definitions For the purposes of this Regulation, the following definitions apply: (1) ‘foreign direct investment’ means an investment of any kind by a foreign investor aiming to establish or to maintain lasting and direct links between the foreign investor and the entrepreneur to whom or the undertaking to which the capital is made available in order to carry on an economic activity in a Member State, including investments which enable effective participation in the management or control of a company carrying out an economic activity; (2) ‘foreign investor’ means a natural person of a third country or an undertaking of a third country, intending to make or having made a foreign direct investment; (3) ‘screening’ means a procedure allowing to assess, investigate, authorise, condition, prohibit or unwind foreign direct investments; (4) ‘screening mechanism’ means an instrument of general application, such as a law or regulation, and accompanying administrative requirements, implementing rules or guidelines, setting out the terms, conditions and procedures to assess, investigate, authorise, condition, prohibit or unwind foreign direct investments on grounds of security or public order; (5) ‘foreign direct investment undergoing screening’ means a foreign direct investment undergoing a formal assessment or investigation pursuant to a screening mechanism; (6) ‘screening decision’ means a measure adopted in application of a screening mechanism; (7) ‘undertaking of a third country’ means an undertaking constituted or otherwise organised under the laws of a third country.
descrizione_funzionale: Definitional provision that fixes the meaning of the key terms used throughout the framework, thereby determining the scope of the rules, the actors covered, and the procedural triggers and outcomes. It operates at a high but not foundational level: broadly applicable across the whole act, yet still technical and interpretative, because it supplies the vocabulary that other provisions rely on rather than imposing direct substantive obligations itself.

testo_originale: Article 3 Screening mechanisms of Member States
descrizione_funzionale: Provision that identifies the national screening arrangements covered by the framework and, by implication, marks the point at which the common rules become relevant. It operates at a structural, intermediate level: not a broad guiding principle, but a gateway rule that delineates the regulatory field and sets the stage for the more detailed obligations that follow.

testo_originale: 1. In accordance with this Regulation, Member States may maintain, amend or adopt mechanisms to screen foreign direct investments in their territory on the grounds of security or public order.
descrizione_funzionale: Enabling clause that authorises Member States to keep, change, or create domestic screening mechanisms, while tying that power to the Regulation’s conditions and limiting it to security or public-order grounds. It operates at a relatively high but not foundational level: it structures national regulatory competence within the framework rather than laying down a detailed procedural rule or a case-specific trigger.

testo_originale: 2. Rules and procedures related to screening mechanisms, including relevant timeframes, shall be transparent and not discriminate between third countries. In particular, Member States shall set out the circumstances triggering the screening, the grounds for screening and the applicable detailed procedural rules.
descrizione_funzionale: Operative rule laying down the quality requirements for screening arrangements and specifying the core elements that must be made public and applied consistently, including the triggers, grounds, and procedural steps. It sits at a relatively detailed level: not a general principle of the whole framework, but a concrete implementation rule that structures how national screening systems must be designed and administered.

testo_originale: 3. Member States shall apply timeframes under their screening mechanisms. The screening mechanisms shall allow Member States to take into account the comments of other Member States referred to in Article 6 and 7 and the opinions of the Commission referred to in Articles 6, 7 and
descrizione_funzionale: Operational rule requiring national screening systems to include time limits and to be designed so that external comments and institutional opinions can be considered in the decision-making process. It sits at a fairly specific, implementing level: not a general principle, but a procedural coordination rule that shapes how a particular type of review must function.

testo_originale: 4. Confidential information, including commercially-sensitive information, made available to the Member State undertaking the screening shall be protected.
descrizione_funzionale: Protective rule imposing a duty of confidentiality on authorities handling information in the screening process, ensuring that sensitive material disclosed in that context is safeguarded. It operates at a relatively specific, operational level: not a broad organising principle, but a targeted safeguard that applies whenever such information is made available during the procedure.

testo_originale: 5. Foreign investors and the undertakings concerned shall have the possibility to seek recourse against screening decisions of the national authorities.
descrizione_funzionale: Remedial clause guaranteeing an avenue of challenge against screening decisions, thereby constraining administrative discretion by requiring that affected parties be able to contest the outcome before the competent system. It operates at an operational level: important for the framework’s fairness and legality, but limited to the specific post-decision stage rather than laying down a general substantive rule.

testo_originale: 6. Member States which have a screening mechanism in place shall maintain, amend or adopt measures necessary to identify and prevent circumvention of the screening mechanisms and screening decisions.
descrizione_funzionale: Obligation-imposing provision requiring Member States with an existing screening mechanism to keep it effective by maintaining, adjusting, or introducing measures that detect and block evasion of screening rules and decisions. It operates at an operational level: not a general principle, but a targeted rule that secures the practical integrity of the screening system against обход strategies.

testo_originale: 7. Member States shall notify the Commission of their existing screening mechanisms by 10 May
descrizione_funzionale: Notification obligation requiring Member States to inform the Commission of pre-existing screening mechanisms by a fixed deadline, thereby enabling transparency and coordination within the framework. It operates at an intermediate, administrative level: not a broad principle, but a concrete procedural rule that supports the system’s functioning through a one-time reporting duty.

testo_originale: 2019. Member States shall notify the Commission of any newly adopted screening mechanism or any amendment to an existing screening mechanism within 30 days of the entry into force of the newly adopted screening mechanism or of any amendment to an existing screening mechanism.
descrizione_funzionale: Notification obligation requiring Member States to inform the Commission whenever they introduce or amend a screening mechanism, and to do so within a fixed 30-day period. It is an operational compliance rule at a fairly specific level, implementing the framework’s information-sharing architecture through a precise procedural deadline.

testo_originale: 8. No later than three months after having received the notifications referred to in paragraph 7, the Commission shall make publicly available a list of Member States' screening mechanisms. The Commission shall keep that list up to date.
descrizione_funzionale: Publicity and maintenance clause requiring the Commission to publish, within a fixed deadline, an official list of national screening mechanisms and to keep it current. It operates at an operational level, translating the notification system into an administrative transparency duty with a narrow, technical function rather than laying down any broad substantive rule.

testo_originale: Article 4 Factors that may be taken into consideration by Member States or the Commission
descrizione_funzionale: Provision identifying the substantive factors that may guide an assessment and thereby justify or shape a screening decision, while leaving the actual weight of each factor to the competent authority’s judgment. It operates at an intermediate, framework-setting level: more concrete than a general objective, but still broad and open-textured rather than a narrow rule for a single case.

testo_originale: 1. In determining whether a foreign direct investment is likely to affect security or public order, Member States and the Commission may consider its potential effects on, inter alia:
descrizione_funzionale: This provision supplies an interpretive yardstick for assessing whether a transaction may trigger concern, by authorising authorities to take account of specified potential effects when judging risk. It sits at an intermediate level of abstraction: not a broad statement of purpose, but not a narrow mechanical rule either, instead guiding the evaluative step that structures the screening exercise.

testo_originale: (a) critical infrastructure, whether physical or virtual, including energy, transport, water, health, communications, media, data processing or storage, aerospace, defence, electoral or financial infrastructure, and sensitive facilities, as well as land and real estate crucial for the use of such infrastructure;

testo_originale: (c) supply of critical inputs, including energy or raw materials, as well as food security;
descrizione_funzionale: Defines one of the substantive risk factors to be taken into account when assessing whether an investment may affect protected interests, by identifying the supply of critical inputs as a relevant criterion. It operates at a mid-to-low level of abstraction: not a general principle, but a concrete substantive indicator that helps structure case-by-case screening decisions.

testo_originale: (d) access to sensitive information, including personal data, or the ability to control such information; or
descrizione_funzionale: Operative criterion identifying one of the concrete risk factors that may be taken into account when assessing whether an investment could affect protected interests, by focusing on access to or control over sensitive information. It sits at a fairly specific, application-oriented level: not a general principle, but a targeted element that helps trigger and shape case-by-case assessment within the broader screening framework.

testo_originale: (e) the freedom and pluralism of the media.
descrizione_funzionale: Substantive criterion identifying a protected public-interest value that can justify scrutiny or intervention when assessing whether an external investment may affect the order’s core interests. It operates at a relatively high level of abstraction within the framework, as one element in a broader list of general considerations rather than a technical rule or procedural step.

testo_originale: 2. In determining whether a foreign direct investment is likely to affect security or public order, Member States and the Commission may also take into account, in particular:
descrizione_funzionale: Discretion-guiding criterion that authorises national authorities and the Commission to consider additional listed factors when assessing whether an investment may threaten protected interests; it does not itself decide the outcome, but shapes the evaluative method. It sits at an intermediate level of abstraction: more specific than the general assessment rule, yet still open-textured and adaptable, functioning as a non-exhaustive interpretive aid for individual cases.

testo_originale: (a) whether the foreign investor is directly or indirectly controlled by the government, including state bodies or armed forces, of a third country, including through ownership structure or significant funding;
descrizione_funzionale: Criterion identifying a relevant risk indicator to be assessed when deciding whether an investment may warrant closer scrutiny. It operates at a fairly concrete, operational level, supplying a specific factual test within a broader evaluative framework rather than laying down a general principle.

testo_originale: (b) whether the foreign investor has already been involved in activities affecting security or public order in a Member State; or
descrizione_funzionale: This criterion functions as a substantive risk-assessment factor, allowing the competent authority to take into account the investor’s prior conduct when judging whether an intervention is warranted. It sits at an operational level: not a general principle, but a specific evaluative element within a broader screening test that helps calibrate the decision in individual cases.

testo_originale: (c) whether there is a serious risk that the foreign investor engages in illegal or criminal activities.
descrizione_funzionale: Risk-assessment criterion identifying one of the factors that may justify closer scrutiny of an investment, by requiring authorities to consider whether the investor presents a serious risk of unlawful conduct. It operates at an operational level within the broader assessment framework, supplying a specific evaluative trigger rather than a general principle or a procedural rule.

testo_originale: 1. By 31 March of each year, Member States shall submit to the Commission an annual report covering the preceding calendar year, which shall include aggregated information on foreign direct investments that took place in their territory, on the basis of information available to them, as well as aggregated information on the requests received from other Member States pursuant to Articles 6(6) and 7(5).
descrizione_funzionale: Reporting obligation requiring Member States to transmit a yearly consolidated account to the Commission, including specified categories of aggregated information and cross-border requests. It operates at an operational level: a concrete administrative duty that implements the framework’s information-sharing architecture through a precise deadline and defined content.

testo_originale: 2. For each reporting period, Member States that maintain screening mechanisms shall, in addition to the information referred to in paragraph 1, provide aggregated information on the application of their screening mechanisms.
descrizione_funzionale: Reporting obligation requiring Member States that keep such mechanisms in place to supply aggregated information for each reporting period, thereby operationalising the broader transparency and monitoring architecture. It sits at a fairly specific, implementation-focused level: not a general principle, but a targeted administrative rule that adds a concrete data-delivery duty to an existing reporting framework.

testo_originale: 3. The Commission shall provide an annual report on the implementation of this Regulation to the European Parliament and to the Council. That report shall be made public.
descrizione_funzionale: Reporting clause imposing an ongoing accountability duty on the Commission and requiring public disclosure of the results, thereby ensuring institutional oversight and transparency in the operation of the framework. It is a relatively specific procedural rule: it does not create substantive rights or criteria, but implements a recurring administrative obligation that applies throughout the life of the regime.

testo_originale: 4. The European Parliament may invite the Commission to a meeting of its committee responsible to present and explain systemic issues related to the implementation of this Regulation.
descrizione_funzionale: Procedural coordination clause enabling the European Parliament to summon the Commission before the competent committee to present and explain systemic implementation issues, thereby creating an accountability and information channel within the institutional framework. It operates at a relatively specific, operational level: not laying down substantive rules, but arranging how oversight and dialogue function in practice when broader implementation concerns arise.

testo_originale: Article 6 Cooperation mechanism in relation to foreign direct investments undergoing screening
descrizione_funzionale: Structural provision establishing a coordinated cooperation mechanism among authorities when an investment is being examined, thereby organising how information and input are exchanged within the framework. It sits at an intermediate level of abstraction: not a broad policy statement, but not a narrow technical trigger either, instead setting the operative architecture for a recurring class of cases.

testo_originale: 1. Member States shall notify the Commission and the other Member States of any foreign direct investment in their territory that is undergoing screening by providing the information referred to in Article 9(2) of this Regulation as soon as possible. The notification may include a list of Member States whose security or public order is deemed likely to be affected. As part of the notification, and where applicable, the Member State undertaking the screening shall endeavour to indicate whether it considers that the foreign direct investment undergoing screening is likely to fall within the scope of Regulation (EC) No 139/2004.
descrizione_funzionale: Notification rule imposing an information-sharing duty on the screening authority and, where relevant, a duty to flag the possible relevance of another regime; it also cross-references the required content of the notice and allows an optional identification of affected peers. It operates at an operational, mid-level of abstraction: not a general principle, but a concrete procedural mechanism that activates whenever a screening is underway.

testo_originale: 2. Where a Member State considers that a foreign direct investment undergoing screening in another Member State is likely to affect its security or public order, or has information relevant for such screening, it may provide comments to the Member State undertaking the screening. The Member State providing comments shall send those comments to the Commission simultaneously. The Commission shall notify the other Member States that comments were provided.
descrizione_funzionale: Cooperative procedural clause enabling one authority to submit observations to another when a cross-border screening may implicate its security or public order, while also imposing parallel notification duties on the Commission. It operates at an intermediate, operational level: not a broad principle, but a concrete coordination mechanism that activates in a defined situation and structures inter-institutional communication.

testo_originale: 3. Where the Commission considers that a foreign direct investment undergoing screening is likely to affect security or public order in more than one Member State, or has relevant information in relation to that foreign direct investment, it may issue an opinion addressed to the Member State undertaking the screening. The Commission may issue an opinion irrespective of whether other Member States have provided comments. The Commission may issue an opinion following comments from other Member States. The Commission shall issue such opinion where justified, after at least one third of Member States consider that a foreign direct investment is likely to affect their security or public order. The Commission shall notify the other Member States that an opinion was issued.
descrizione_funzionale: Discretionary and, in one case, mandatory intervention clause that authorises the central institution to issue an opinion to the screening authority when a cross-border risk or relevant information is present, while also requiring action once a specified collective trigger is met; it additionally imposes a notification duty to the other participating authorities. The provision sits at an intermediate, coordinating level: it does not define the underlying risk concept, but it structures how institutional input is channelled and when the power must be exercised.

testo_originale: 4. A Member State which duly considers that a foreign direct investment in its territory is likely to affect its security or public order may request the Commission to issue an opinion or other Member States to provide comments.
descrizione_funzionale: Enabling clause that opens a formal consultation channel, allowing a Member State to trigger an EU-level opinion and invite observations from other Member States where a specific investment is seen as potentially affecting security or public order. It operates at an intermediate, procedural level: not a general principle, but a targeted mechanism that activates only when the stated risk assessment is made.

testo_originale: 5. The comments referred to in paragraph 2 and the opinions referred to in paragraph 3 shall be duly justified.
descrizione_funzionale: This provision imposes a reason-giving requirement on the comments and opinions exchanged under the preceding paragraphs, ensuring that any position taken is accompanied by an articulated justification. It operates at an operational, procedural level: a targeted rule that governs how a specific step in the framework must be carried out, rather than setting any broad substantive standard.

testo_originale: 6. No later than 15 calendar days following the receipt of the information referred to in paragraph 1, other Member States and the Commission shall notify the Member State undertaking the screening of their intention to provide comments pursuant to paragraph 2 or an opinion pursuant to paragraph
descrizione_funzionale: Procedural deadline provision that triggers a time-bound notification duty for other institutions to signal whether they will participate in the coordinated review process, thereby structuring the exchange of information and comments within the screening mechanism. It operates at a fairly technical, operational level: it does not create the underlying power to comment or opine, but fixes the narrow temporal condition for exercising that existing role.

testo_originale: 3. The notification may include a request for additional information to the information referred to in paragraph
descrizione_funzionale: Ancillary procedural clause allowing the notifying party to bundle a request for supplementary information with the notification itself, thereby shaping how the information-gathering phase is initiated and managed. It operates at a fairly technical, implementation-oriented level, refining the mechanics of the procedure rather than laying down any broad substantive rule.

testo_originale: 1. Any request for additional information shall be duly justified, limited to information necessary to provide comments pursuant to paragraph 2 or to issue an opinion pursuant to paragraph 3, proportionate to the purpose of the request and not unduly burdensome for the Member State undertaking the screening. It operates at a fairly detailed, operational level, refining how the information-exchange mechanism must be carried out in a specific procedural setting rather than laying down a general principle for the whole framework.

testo_originale: 7. Comments referred to in paragraph 2 or opinions referred to in paragraph 3 shall be addressed to the Member State undertaking the screening and shall be sent to it within a reasonable period of time, and in any case no later than 35 calendar days following receipt of the information referred to in paragraph
descrizione_funzionale: Procedural rule governing the circulation and timing of intergovernmental observations within a screening process, requiring them to be directed to the authority conducting the review and delivered within a fixed outer deadline. It operates at a fairly technical, implementation-focused level, translating a broader cooperation mechanism into a concrete time limit and routing requirement for a specific stage of the procedure.

Notwithstanding the first subparagraph, if additional information was requested pursuant to paragraph 6, such comments or opinions shall be issued no later than 20 calendar days following receipt of the additional information or the notification pursuant to Article 9(5). Notwithstanding paragraph 6, the Commission may issue an opinion following comments from other Member States where possible within the deadlines referred to in this paragraph, and in any case no later than five calendar days after those deadlines have expired.
