For the purposes of this Regulation, a subcontractor or supplier shall be deemed to be main where their participation ensures key elements of the contract performance and in any case where the economic share of their contribution exceeds 20 % of the value of the submitted tender.
descrizione_funzionale: Operative provision extending a notification duty to a defined set of market participants and then supplying a legal test for when supporting contractors or suppliers count as “main” for that purpose. It sits at a fairly technical, implementation-focused level: it does not set the general policy, but calibrates the reach of an existing obligation through a precise applicability rule and a quantitative threshold.

testo_originale: 6. On behalf of groups of economic operators, main subcontractors and main suppliers, the main contractor within the meaning of Directives 2014/24/EU and 2014/25/EU or main concessionaire within the meaning of Directive 2014/23/EU shall ensure the submission of the notification or declaration. For the purposes of Article 33, the main contractor or main concessionaire is responsible only for the veracity of data linked to its own foreign financial contributions.
descrizione_funzionale: Allocates the procedural duty to file the notification or declaration to the lead contracting party in a chain of economic operators, while limiting that party’s responsibility for accuracy to the information tied to its own contributions. It operates at a fairly specific, operational level, translating a broader reporting obligation into a concrete allocation of responsibility for a defined category of actors.

testo_originale: 7. Where the contracting authority or contracting entity examining tenders suspects the presence of foreign subsidies, although a declaration was submitted, it shall communicate such suspicions to the Commission without delay. Without prejudice to the powers of contracting authorities or contracting entities, laid down in Directives 2014/24/EU and 2014/25/EU, to examine whether a tender is abnormally low, the contracting authority or contracting entity shall not perform an assessment of whether a tender is abnormally low where such an assessment would be initiated on the suspicions indicating a possible presence of foreign subsidies alone. Where the Commission concludes that there is no unduly advantageous tender within the meaning of this Regulation, it shall inform the relevant contracting authority or contracting entity thereof. Other legal or natural persons may report to the Commission any information relating to foreign subsidies distorting the internal market and may communicate any suspicions that a false declaration has possibly been made.
descrizione_funzionale: Operative coordination rule allocating responsibilities between the contracting authority or entity and the Commission when suspicions arise, while also preserving the authority’s separate power to assess abnormally low tenders under the referenced directives. It sits at a fairly specific, implementation-oriented level: it governs a narrow procedural sequence triggered by suspicion, including mandatory notification, a restriction on parallel assessment, and a follow-up communication by the Commission, rather than laying down a general principle for the whole framework.

testo_originale: 8. Without prejudice of the possibility for the Commission to start an ex officio procedure, where the Commission suspects that an economic operator may have benefitted from foreign subsidies in the three years prior to the submission of the tender or request to participate in the public procurement procedure, it may before the award of the contract request the notification of the foreign financial contributions provided by third countries to that economic operator in any public procurement procedure which are not notifiable under Article 28(1) or fall within the scope of Article 30(4). If the Commission has required the notification of such a financial contribution, the financial contribution shall be deemed to be a notifiable foreign financial contribution in a public procurement procedure and be subject to the provisions set out in Chapter 4.
descrizione_funzionale: Conditional intervention clause empowering the Commission to require disclosure of specified financial contributions before an award decision, and to reclassify those contributions as formally notifiable once that request is made. It operates at an intermediate, operational level: more specific than the general framework rules, but still setting a procedural trigger and legal consequence for a defined class of cases rather than a mere technical detail.

testo_originale: Article 30 Procedural rules applicable to the preliminary review and the in-depth investigation of notified financial contributions in public procurement procedures
descrizione_funzionale: Procedural provision laying down the rules that govern how the preliminary review and any deeper examination are to be conducted in a specific notification-based context, thereby structuring the decision-making process rather than creating the substantive test itself. It operates at an intermediate, operational level: more concrete than the framework’s general principles, but still broad enough to organise the entire sequence of steps for this category of cases.

testo_originale: 1. Articles 10, 11 (1), (3) and (4), 13, 14, 15, 16, 18 and 23 shall apply to notified financial contributions in public procurement procedures.
descrizione_funzionale: This provision extends a selected set of existing procedural and substantive rules to a particular category of notified financial contributions when they arise in public procurement procedures, thereby cross-applying the framework to a defined enforcement context. It operates at a fairly specific, operational level: not as a general principle, but as a technical rule that determines the reach of several provisions in one narrowly identified situation.

testo_originale: 2. The Commission shall carry out a preliminary review no later than 20 working days after it receives a complete notification. In duly justified cases, the Commission may extend this time limit by 10 working days once.
descrizione_funzionale: Procedural timing rule that obliges the authority to complete an initial assessment within a fixed period after receiving a complete filing, while also allowing a single, justified extension. It operates at a fairly specific, operational level, implementing a narrow case-management detail that structures the pace of the review without determining the substantive outcome.

testo_originale: 3. The Commission shall decide whether to initiate an in-depth investigation within the time limit for completing the preliminary review and inform the economic operator concerned and the contracting authority or the contracting entity without delay.
descrizione_funzionale: This provision allocates a procedural decision-making power to the Commission, requiring it to choose whether to move from an initial review to a more intensive examination and to notify the relevant parties promptly. It operates at an operational level: a concrete case-management rule that governs the transition between stages of the procedure, rather than a broad principle or a technical detail.

testo_originale: 4. Where the Commission had closed a preliminary review without adopting a decision and receives new information leading it to suspect that a submitted notification or declaration was incomplete, or where such a notification or declaration is not transferred to the Commission, it may request additional information in accordance with Article 29(4). The Commission may reopen a preliminary review based on this new information. Where the preliminary review is initiated under this Chapter, and without prejudice to the possibility to initiate a preliminary review under Chapter 2, as the need may arise, the starting point for the determination of the duration of the preliminary review is the receipt of the new notification or declaration by the Commission.
descrizione_funzionale: Procedural reopening clause that allows the authority to seek further information and revive an earlier review when new material suggests the original filing was incomplete or never properly received; it also fixes the temporal starting point for calculating the review period in that renewed process. Its role is operational and fairly specific, because it regulates a narrow remedial situation within the broader enforcement architecture rather than laying down a general principle.

testo_originale: 5. The Commission may adopt a decision closing the in-depth investigation no later than 110 working days after it has received the complete notification. This period may be extended once by 20 working days, after consultation with the contracting authority or contracting entity, in duly justified exceptional cases including the investigations referred to in paragraph 6 or in cases referred to in Article 16(1), points
descrizione_funzionale: Operative time-limit clause governing the conclusion of the in-depth review, coupled with a discretionary extension mechanism and a consultation requirement in exceptional cases. It sits at a highly specific, technical level, implementing a narrow procedural rule that controls when the authority must close the examination rather than laying down any broader substantive standard.

testo_originale: 6. By way of derogation from paragraph 2, where the public procurement procedure is a multi-stage procedure, the Commission shall examine the complete notification submitted with the request to participate within 20 working days from the receipt of that notification, without closing the preliminary review or reaching a decision on opening an in-depth investigation. After the deadline of 20 working days elapses, the preliminary review shall be suspended until the submission of a final tender or a tender in the case of a restricted procedure. Once the tender or final tender containing a complete updated notification is submitted, the preliminary review shall be resumed and the Commission has 20 working days to finalise it, taking into account any additional information. The Commission shall adopt a decision closing any ensuing in-depth investigation within 90 working days from the submission of the completed updated notification.
descrizione_funzionale: Exception-based procedural rule that recalibrates the review timetable for a particular multi-stage procurement setting, splitting the examination into distinct phases and fixing the points at which review is suspended, resumed, and concluded. It operates at a fairly technical, implementation-focused level: specific and time-bound, refining the general review mechanism rather than laying down a broad substantive principle.

testo_originale: Article 31 Commission decisions
descrizione_funzionale: Operative provision that confers decisional authority on the Commission, enabling it to adopt binding determinations under the framework and thereby translate the regime into concrete administrative action. It sits at an intermediate, institutional level: more specific than the act’s general principles, but still a structural rule governing how the framework is applied in practice rather than a narrow technical detail.

testo_originale: 1. Where, after an in-depth investigation, the Commission finds that an economic operator benefits from a foreign subsidy distorting the internal market pursuant to Articles 4, 5 and 6, and where the economic operator concerned offers commitments that fully and effectively remedy the distortion in the internal market, it shall adopt an implementing act in the form of a decision with commitments pursuant to Article 11(3). That implementing act shall be adopted in accordance with the advisory procedure referred to in Article 48(2).
descrizione_funzionale: Operative decision-making clause that obliges the authority to convert a completed investigation into a binding act when two cumulative conditions are met: a finding of distortion and the offer of commitments that fully and effectively cure it, while also cross-referencing the procedural route for adoption. It sits at a fairly specific, implementation-oriented level, translating higher-order substantive criteria into a concrete institutional response and procedural form.

testo_originale: 2. Where the economic operator concerned does not offer commitments or where the Commission considers that the commitments referred to in paragraph 1 are neither appropriate nor sufficient to fully and effectively remedy the distortion, the Commission shall adopt an implementing act in the form of a decision prohibiting the award of the contract to the economic operator concerned (‘decision prohibiting the award of the contract’). That implementing act shall be adopted in accordance with the advisory procedure referred to in Article 48(2). Following that decision, the contracting authority or contracting entity shall reject the tender.
descrizione_funzionale: Operative enforcement clause that triggers a mandatory prohibitory decision when remedial commitments are absent or inadequate, and it also directs the contracting authority to reject the tender after that decision. It sits at a highly specific, implementation-focused level, translating a prior assessment into a concrete procedural outcome in a narrowly defined case.

testo_originale: 3. Where, after an in-depth investigation, the Commission does not find that an economic operator benefits from a foreign subsidy distorting the internal market, it shall adopt an implementing act in the form of a decision pursuant to Article 11(4). That implementing act shall be adopted in accordance with the advisory procedure referred to in Article 48(2).
descrizione_funzionale: Operative closure clause that requires the authority, after a full investigation, to formalise a negative finding through a binding implementing decision and to follow a specified committee procedure in doing so. It sits at a fairly concrete, procedural level: it does not set the substantive test itself, but translates the outcome of that test into a mandatory institutional step with a defined decision-making method.

testo_originale: 4. The assessment under Article 6 shall not result in a modification of the tender or final tender submitted by the economic operator that is incompatible with Union law.
descrizione_funzionale: This provision sets a legal limit on the outcome of the assessment by prohibiting any alteration of the tender that would conflict with superior law, thereby constraining the authority’s remedial reach. It operates at a fairly specific, operational level: a narrow safeguard that applies only once the assessment under the referenced article is being used to shape the content of a submitted offer.

testo_originale: Article 32 Evaluations in public procurement procedures involving a notification and suspension of award
descrizione_funzionale: Provision introducing a special evaluative rule for public procurement procedures where a notification and suspension mechanism is triggered, thereby linking the general procurement process to a targeted review step before award. It operates at an intermediate, operational level: more specific than the framework’s general principles, but still structuring how the procedure unfolds in a defined class of cases.

testo_originale: 1. During the preliminary review and the in-depth investigation, all procedural steps in the public procurement procedure may continue, except for the award of the contract.
descrizione_funzionale: Operational rule governing the conduct of an ongoing procedure by allowing it to proceed while carving out one decisive act that must be withheld. It sits at a fairly specific, implementation-oriented level, adjusting the timing and scope of procedural continuity in a narrow investigative context rather than laying down a general principle for the whole framework.

testo_originale: 2. If the Commission decides to open an in-depth investigation pursuant to Article 30(3), the contract shall not be awarded to an economic operator submitting a notification under Article 29 until the Commission takes a decision under Article 31(3) or before the time limits set in Article 30(5) or (6) elapse. If the Commission has not adopted a decision within the applicable time limit, the contract may be awarded to any economic operator, including the economic operator submitting the notification.
descrizione_funzionale: Operative suspension rule that temporarily blocks the award of a contract once a formal in-depth review has been opened, and then lifts that block either when the review ends with a decision or when the relevant deadlines expire. It sits at a highly specific, implementation-focused level, translating the broader review mechanism into a concrete interim consequence for a narrowly defined procedural situation.

testo_originale: 3. Where the contracting authority or contracting entity finds that the most economically advantageous tender was submitted by an economic operator, which submitted a declaration within the meaning of Article 29 and where the Commission has not opened a review in line with Articles 29(8), 30(3) or 30(4), the contract may be awarded to the economic operator submitting such a tender before the Commission takes any of the decisions referred to in Article 31 or before the time limits laid down in Articles 30(2), 30(5) or 30(6) elapse or before the Commission takes any of the decisions referred to in Article 31 regarding other tenders under investigation.
descrizione_funzionale: Conditional award rule allowing the contracting authority or entity to proceed with awarding the contract to the preferred tenderer when specified disclosure and non-intervention conditions are met, even before the supervisory authority has acted or the relevant time limits expire. It is a highly operational, case-specific provision that fine-tunes the timing of the award decision within a narrow procedural sequence rather than laying down a general principle.

testo_originale: 4. Where the Commission adopts a decision in accordance with Article 31(2) concerning a tender which the contracting authority or contracting entity has found to be the most economically advantageous tender, the contract may be awarded to the economic operator not subject to a decision under Article 31(2) having submitted the next best tender.
descrizione_funzionale: Operative allocation rule that determines how the contract may be awarded when the preferred tender is affected by a prior Commission decision, effectively redirecting the award to the next eligible bidder. It sits at a fairly specific, implementation-focused level, applying only in the defined procedural scenario and translating a higher-order control mechanism into a concrete consequence for the award process.

testo_originale: 5. Where the Commission adopts a decision in accordance with Article 31(1) or (3), the contract may be awarded to any economic operator having submitted the most economically advantageous tender, including, to the economic operator having submitted the notification under Article
descrizione_funzionale: Operative fallback rule governing the award of a contract after the authority has taken a decision under the preceding provisions, and it identifies the eligible recipient by reference to the most economically advantageous tender, including the notifying operator. It sits at a fairly specific, implementation-oriented level: it does not set the general regime, but resolves the practical consequence of a particular decision in a defined procedural situation.

testo_originale: 6. The contracting authority or the contracting entity shall inform the Commission without undue delay of any decision relating to the cancellation of the public procurement procedure, the rejection of the tender or request to participate by the economic operator concerned, the submission of a new tender by the economic operator concerned or the award of the contract.
descrizione_funzionale: Procedural notification rule imposing a duty on the contracting authority or entity to promptly inform the Commission of specified outcomes in the procurement process, thereby enabling oversight and follow-up action. It operates at a fairly granular, operational level: it does not create the underlying decision-making power itself, but implements a narrow reporting obligation triggered by clearly defined procedural events.

testo_originale: 7. The principles governing public procurement procedures, including the principles of proportionality, non-discrimination, equal treatment, transparency and competition, shall be observed as regards all economic operators involved in the public procurement procedure. The investigation of foreign subsidies pursuant to this Regulation shall not result in the contracting authority or the contracting entity treating the economic operators concerned in a way that is contrary to those principles. Environmental, social and labour requirements shall apply to economic operators in accordance with Directives 2014/23/EU, 2014/24/EU and 2014/25/EU, or other Union law.
descrizione_funzionale: This provision functions as a safeguard clause that imports and reaffirms general procedural principles, while also limiting how the investigation may affect the treatment of participants and cross-referencing external rules on environmental, social and labour requirements. It sits at a relatively high but not foundational level: it does not create the investigation mechanism itself, but constrains its operation by embedding it within broader, pre-existing procedural standards.

testo_originale: 8. Time limits referred to in this Chapter shall begin on the working day following that of the receipt of the notification or of the adoption of the relevant Commission decision.
descrizione_funzionale: Procedural timing rule that determines when the deadlines in this chapter start to run, thereby organising the temporal operation of the notification and decision-making process. It is a narrow implementing detail with limited scope, applying only to the calculation of time limits in this specific chapter rather than setting any broader substantive rule.

testo_originale: Article 33 Fines and periodic penalty payments applicable to financial contributions in the context of public procurement procedures
descrizione_funzionale: Operative enforcement clause that authorises the imposition of monetary penalties and recurring coercive payments where a party fails to comply with obligations linked to the relevant procedure, thereby giving the regime its sanctioning teeth. It sits at a highly specific, implementation-focused level: not a general principle, but a targeted mechanism that activates only in the defined procedural context and supports compliance through deterrence.

testo_originale: 1. The Commission may impose fines or periodic penalty payments as set out in Article
descrizione_funzionale: Empowerment clause conferring on the Commission the authority to impose coercive financial penalties, while directing the reader to the detailed conditions and limits laid down elsewhere in the act. It operates at an intermediate, institutional level: not a general principle, but a targeted enforcement mechanism that activates the sanctioning machinery without itself specifying the full procedural or quantitative rules.

testo_originale: 2. The Commission may, by decision, also impose fines upon the economic operators concerned that do not exceed 1 % of their aggregate turnover in the preceding financial year, where those economic operators intentionally or negligently supply incorrect or misleading information in a notification or declaration pursuant to Article 29 or in a supplement thereto.
descrizione_funzionale: Sanctioning provision conferring on the Commission the power to impose a monetary penalty when an operator provides incorrect or misleading information in a notification, declaration, or supplement, and tying that power to a specified turnover-based ceiling. It operates at a fairly specific, enforcement-oriented level: not a general principle, but a targeted rule that activates in a defined procedural context and calibrates the consequence by reference to a precise quantitative limit.

testo_originale: 3. The Commission may, by decision, impose fines upon the economic operators concerned that do not exceed 10 % of their aggregate turnover in the preceding financial year where those economic operators, intentionally or negligently:
descrizione_funzionale: Sanctioning clause conferring on the Commission the power to impose monetary penalties on the operators concerned when they act intentionally or negligently in breach of the relevant obligations. It operates at an operational level: a concrete enforcement mechanism tied to a specific misconduct condition and capped by a precise turnover-based ceiling.

testo_originale: (a) fail to notify foreign financial contributions in accordance with Article 29 during the public procurement procedure;
descrizione_funzionale: Operative prohibition clause identifying a specific procedural breach that triggers adverse consequences in the course of a procurement process, by treating the omission of a required notification as a non-compliant act. It sits at a highly concrete level, implementing a narrow enforcement rule that applies only when a defined reporting duty is ignored in that particular procedure.

testo_originale: (b) circumvent or attempt to circumvent the notification requirements, as referred to in Article 39(1).
descrizione_funzionale: Operative anti-avoidance clause that extends the rule’s reach to conduct designed to evade the notification duty, thereby preserving the effectiveness of the reporting regime and supporting enforcement. It sits at a fairly specific, implementation-focused level: not a general principle, but a targeted rule addressing a particular form of non-compliance within the broader procedural framework.

testo_originale: Article 34 Relationship between procedures 1. A financial contribution notified in the context of a concentration under Article 21 or in the context of a public procurement under Article 29 may be relevant to and assessed under this Regulation in relation to another economic activity. 2. A financial contribution assessed in the context of an ex officio procedure in relation to a specific economic activity under Article 10 or Article 11 may be relevant to and assessed under this Regulation in relation to another economic activity.
descrizione_funzionale: Coordination clause linking parallel procedural tracks and allowing information gathered in one notification or ex officio assessment to be reused when examining a different economic activity, thereby avoiding fragmented treatment of the same underlying contribution. It operates at an intermediate, structural level: not a broad principle, but a rule that organises how separate procedures interact and how their findings may carry over across cases.

testo_originale: Article 35 Communication of information
descrizione_funzionale: Operative disclosure clause requiring the transmission of information to the competent authority, thereby enabling oversight and follow-up within the enforcement architecture. It sits at a practical, implementation-oriented level: not a broad principle, but a procedural rule that supports the framework by ensuring the flow of relevant data in a defined context.

testo_originale: 1. Where a Member State considers that a foreign subsidy may exist and may distort the internal market, it shall transfer information thereon to the Commission. The Commission may on the basis of that information decide to start a preliminary review pursuant to Article 10, or request a notification pursuant to Article 21(5) or Article 29(8).
descrizione_funzionale: Procedural referral clause that channels a Member State’s suspicion to the central authority and, on that basis, enables the latter to choose between opening an initial examination or requiring a formal filing. It operates at an intermediate, operational level: not a broad principle, but a coordination rule that triggers specific follow-up steps once a defined suspicion threshold is reached.

testo_originale: 2. A natural or legal person or association may communicate to the Commission any information it may have about foreign subsidies that may distort the internal market. The Commission may on the basis of that information decide to start a preliminary review pursuant to Article 10, or request a notification pursuant to Article 21(5) or Article 29(8).
descrizione_funzionale: Enabling and informational clause that opens a channel for private parties to alert the authority and, on that basis, allows the authority to trigger further action by initiating a preliminary review or requiring a formal notification. It operates at an intermediate, operational level: not a broad principle, but a procedural gateway that connects external information to the start of specific enforcement steps.

testo_originale: 3. The Commission shall make accessible to Member States and the contracting authorities or contracting entities concerned, on a dedicated electronic database, the non-confidential versions of all decisions adopted under this Regulation.
descrizione_funzionale: Operative transparency and information-sharing rule requiring the Commission to publish non-confidential decision texts in a dedicated electronic repository and to circulate them to the relevant public bodies. It sits at a practical implementation level, translating the framework’s general decision-making powers into a specific dissemination mechanism that supports consistency and awareness across the system.

testo_originale: Article 36 Market investigation
descrizione_funzionale: Provision opening a dedicated investigative mechanism, authorising the competent authority to examine market conditions and gather the factual basis needed for later action. It sits at an intermediate-to-specific level: more than a general principle, but still a structural rule that enables enforcement by setting up a targeted tool for particular cases.

testo_originale: 1. Where the information available to the Commission substantiates a reasonable suspicion that foreign subsidies in a particular sector, for a particular type of economic activity or based on a particular subsidy instrument may distort the internal market, the Commission may conduct a market investigation into the particular sector, the particular type of economic activity or into the use of the subsidy instrument concerned. In the course of that market investigation, the Commission may require the undertakings or associations of undertakings concerned to supply the necessary information and may carry out the necessary inspections. The Commission may also request Member States or the third country concerned to supply information.
descrizione_funzionale: Discretionary investigative power triggered by a substantiated reasonable suspicion, allowing the authority to open a sector-, activity-, or instrument-specific inquiry and to compel information and inspections from relevant actors. It operates at an intermediate, operational level: more specific than the framework’s general principles, but still broad enough to organise how the authority can gather facts across a defined range of cases.

testo_originale: 2. The Commission shall, where relevant, publish a report on the results of its market investigation into particular sectors, particular types of economic activity or particular subsidy instruments and seek comments.
descrizione_funzionale: Procedural transparency clause requiring the Commission, where appropriate, to disclose the outcome of a sectoral or instrument-specific investigation and invite stakeholder observations. It operates at an intermediate, operational level: not a broad empowering principle, but a targeted rule that governs how a particular investigative step is followed through in practice.

testo_originale: 3. The Commission may use the information obtained from such market investigations in the framework of procedures under this Regulation.
descrizione_funzionale: Enabling clause authorising the Commission to reuse information gathered in one investigative track for other procedures under the same act, thereby linking separate enforcement pathways and supporting administrative efficiency. It operates at an intermediate, operational level: not a broad principle, but a procedural coordination rule that applies whenever information from a market investigation is carried over into a subsequent case.

testo_originale: 4. Articles 13, 14, 15 and 17 shall apply to market investigations.
descrizione_funzionale: This cross-referencing clause extends the procedural and investigative rules laid down in the cited provisions to the separate category of market investigations, thereby integrating them into the broader enforcement architecture. It operates at a fairly specific, operational level: not creating a new rule itself, but directing how existing rules are to be applied in a defined procedural context.

testo_originale: Article 37 Third-country dialogue
descrizione_funzionale: Provision establishing a structured dialogue mechanism with third countries, enabling the institutions to engage externally on matters arising under the regime and to support its practical operation through cooperation rather than coercion. It sits at an intermediate, coordinating level: more specific than the act’s general objectives, but still broad enough to organise how the framework interacts with outside actors across a range of situations.

testo_originale: 1. Where, following a market investigation pursuant to Article 36, the Commission suspects the existence of repeated foreign subsidies distorting the internal market, or where several enforcement actions under this Regulation identify foreign subsidies distorting the internal market granted by the same third country, the Commission may engage in a dialogue with the third country concerned, to explore options aimed at obtaining the cessation or modification of such subsidies with a view to eliminating their distortive effects on the internal market. The Commission shall inform the European Parliament and the Council of any relevant developments.
descrizione_funzionale: Conditional empowerment clause authorising the Commission to open a cooperative dialogue with a third country when repeated or recurring enforcement findings point to a pattern of distortive support, and requiring institutional reporting on developments. It sits at an intermediate, operational level: more specific than the general enforcement architecture, but still framing a flexible response mechanism rather than prescribing a rigid, case-by-case procedure.

testo_originale: 2. That third-country dialogue shall not prevent the Commission from taking action under this Regulation. Individual measures adopted pursuant to this Regulation shall not be addressed within that dialogue.
descrizione_funzionale: This provision preserves the Commission’s independent enforcement authority by making clear that a parallel dialogue with a third country cannot suspend or displace action under the Regulation, and that individual measures are excluded from that discussion. It operates at an intermediate, coordinating level: not a broad principle for the whole framework, but a structural rule safeguarding the autonomy of the enforcement mechanism in a specific procedural setting.

testo_originale: 1. The powers of the Commission under Articles 10 and 11 shall be subject to a limitation period of 10 years, starting on the day on which a foreign subsidy is granted to an undertaking. Any action taken by the Commission under Article 10, 13, 14 or 15 with respect to a foreign subsidy shall interrupt the limitation period. After each interruption, the limitation period of 10 years shall start to run afresh.
descrizione_funzionale: Time-bar clause that limits the Commission’s ability to act under the specified provisions, while also defining the events that interrupt and restart the clock. It operates at a fairly technical, implementation-oriented level: a precise procedural safeguard that applies only in the narrow context of enforcement over a defined period.

testo_originale: 2. The powers of the Commission to impose fines or periodic penalty payments under Articles 17, 26 and 33 shall be subject to a limitation period of three years, starting on the day on which the infringement referred to in Article 17, 26 or 33 took place. In the case of continuing or repeated infringements, the limitation period shall start on the day on which the infringement ceases. Any action taken by the Commission with respect to an infringement referred to in Articles 17, 26 or 33 shall interrupt the limitation period for the imposition of fines or periodic penalty payments. After each interruption, the limitation period of three years shall start to run afresh.
descrizione_funzionale: Operative limitation rule that constrains the authority’s sanctioning powers by setting when the time bar begins, how it runs in continuing or repeated cases, and what interrupts it. It sits at a highly technical, implementation-focused level, supplying a precise procedural safeguard for a specific enforcement mechanism rather than a general organizing principle.

testo_originale: 3. The powers of the Commission to enforce decisions imposing fines or periodic penalty payments under Articles 17, 26 and 33 shall be subject to a limitation period of five years, starting on the day on which the Commission decision imposing fines or periodic penalty payments is taken. Any action taken by the Commission, or by a Member State acting upon request of the Commission, intended to enforce payment of the fine or periodic penalty payment shall interrupt that limitation period. After each interruption, the limitation period of five years shall start to run afresh.
descrizione_funzionale: Limitation rule governing the enforcement of monetary penalties, fixing a five-year period from the date of the penalty decision and specifying how interruption restarts the clock. It operates at a highly technical, case-specific level, implementing a procedural constraint on enforcement rather than laying down any broad substantive principle.

testo_originale: 4. The limitation period shall expire at the latest on the day on which twice the amount of time of that limitation period has elapsed provided that the Commission has not:
descrizione_funzionale: Operative time-limit rule that caps the duration of the enforcement period by setting an absolute outer boundary, and it is conditioned on the absence of specified intervening action by the Commission. It sits at a highly technical, implementation-focused level, fine-tuning the mechanics of expiry rather than laying down any broad principle.

testo_originale: (a) taken a decision pursuant to Article 10 or 11 in the instances set out in paragraph 1 of this Article; or
descrizione_funzionale: Cross-reference clause that limits the scope of the provision by tying it to decisions already adopted under specified earlier articles and only in the situations identified in the preceding paragraph. It operates at a narrow, technical level, functioning as a conditional connector within the decision-making architecture rather than laying down an independent rule of general application.

testo_originale: (b) imposed a fine or a periodic penalty payment in the situation set out in paragraph 2 of this Article.
descrizione_funzionale: Operative cross-reference that identifies the specific situation in which a monetary penalty may be imposed, thereby linking the sanctioning power to the conditions laid down earlier in the same article. It sits at a narrow, implementation-focused level, as it does not create the penalty itself but specifies the exact case in which the existing enforcement mechanism applies.

testo_originale: 5. The limitation period shall be suspended for as long as the decision of the Commission is the subject of proceedings pending before the Court of Justice of the European Union.
descrizione_funzionale: Suspension clause governing the running of the limitation period while judicial review of the Commission’s decision is pending, thereby preserving the authority’s ability to act until the challenge is resolved. It operates at a fairly technical, procedural level: a narrow rule that adjusts time limits in a specific litigation scenario rather than laying down a general principle for the whole framework.

testo_originale: Article 39 Anti-circumvention 1. An undertaking shall not arrange financial operations or contracts to circumvent the notification requirements laid down in Article 21(1) and (5) and Article 29(1), (5) and (8). 2. Where the Commission suspects that an undertaking has engaged or is engaging in a practice referred to in paragraph 1, it may require that undertaking to provide any information that the Commission deems necessary to determine whether the undertaking has engaged in or is engaging in the practices referred to in paragraph 1, and may initiate a review pursuant to Article 21(4), or Article 30(4).
descrizione_funzionale: Anti-circumvention rule prohibiting the use of financial arrangements or contracts to evade specified notification duties, and empowering the Commission to demand information and open a review when such evasion is suspected. It operates at an intermediate-to-specific level: not a general principle, but a targeted safeguard that protects the effectiveness of the notification system and activates only where there are signs of avoidance.

testo_originale: Article 40 Publication of decisions 1. The Commission shall make public a summary notice of the decisions adopted pursuant to Article 10(3), point (a), allowing any natural or legal person, Member States or the third country that granted the foreign subsidy, to express their views. 2. The Commission shall publish the decisions adopted pursuant to Article 11(2), (3) and (4), Article 25(3) and (6), and Article 31(1), (2) and (3) in the Official Journal of the European Union . 3. When making public summary notices and decisions, the Commission shall take due account of the legitimate interests of undertakings in the protection of their business secrets and other confidential information.
descrizione_funzionale: Disclosure-and-publication rule that obliges the Commission to make certain decisions and summary notices public, while also opening a channel for interested persons to comment and requiring protection of confidential information. It operates at an intermediate, procedural level: not a broad principle, but a concrete transparency mechanism that structures how decisions are communicated and balanced against secrecy interests.

testo_originale: Article 41 Addressees of decisions
descrizione_funzionale: Operative provision identifying who must be bound by and comply with decisions issued under the act, thereby fixing the addressee of the administrative act and clarifying its legal reach. It sits at a practical, implementation-oriented level: not a broad principle, but a targeted rule that determines the immediate legal effect of decisions in concrete cases.

testo_originale: 1. The Commission shall notify a decision addressed to an undertaking or to an association of undertakings without delay and shall give that undertaking or association of undertakings the opportunity to indicate to the Commission which information in the decision it considers to be confidential.
descrizione_funzionale: Procedural safeguard requiring immediate notification of an individual decision and granting the addressee a chance to identify confidential material before disclosure. It operates at a fairly concrete, operational level: not a broad principle, but a targeted rule governing how the authority must handle confidentiality in a specific decision-making step.

testo_originale: 2. The Commission shall inform the contracting authority or contracting entity concerned about a decision adopted pursuant to Article 31(1) and (3) addressed to an economic operator participating in a public procurement procedure.
descrizione_funzionale: Notification rule imposing an information duty on the Commission vis-à-vis the relevant procurement body when a specified decision has been taken against a participant in the procedure. It operates at a fairly operational level, coordinating the flow of information between institutions in a concrete procedural setting rather than laying down a general principle.

testo_originale: 3. Decisions adopted pursuant to Article 29(4) and Article 31(2) shall be addressed to the contracting authority or contracting entity concerned. The Commission shall provide the economic operator to which the award of the contract is prohibited with a copy of that decision.
descrizione_funzionale: Operative notification rule allocating the addressee of decisions and requiring a copy to be sent to the affected economic operator, thereby ensuring that the prohibition is formally communicated to the relevant parties. It sits at a practical, implementation-focused level: a narrow procedural detail that gives effect to earlier decision-making powers without adding substantive criteria.

testo_originale: Article 42 Disclosure and rights of defence
descrizione_funzionale: Procedural safeguard clause requiring the disclosure of relevant information and preserving the addressee’s ability to respond, thereby structuring how the authority must conduct the process before taking action. It operates at an intermediate level of abstraction: not a broad policy statement, but a general procedural rule that applies across the framework whenever the authority relies on information affecting the parties’ position.

testo_originale: 1. The Commission shall, before adopting a decision pursuant to Articles 11, 12, 17, 18, 25(3), 26, 31 or 33 give the undertaking under investigation the opportunity to submit observations on the grounds on which the Commission intends to adopt its decision.
descrizione_funzionale: Procedural safeguard clause requiring the Commission to hear the undertaking before taking specified decisions, thereby structuring the decision-making process and protecting the right to be heard. It operates at an intermediate level of abstraction: not a general principle for the whole act, but a concrete rule that applies whenever the Commission moves toward one of the listed determinations.

testo_originale: 2. By way of derogation from paragraph 1, a decision pursuant to Article 12 may be taken provisionally, without the undertaking under investigation being given the opportunity to submit its observations beforehand, provided that the Commission gives it that opportunity as soon as possible after having taken its decision.
descrizione_funzionale: Exception clause authorising a provisional decision to be adopted without prior hearing, while preserving the right to be heard immediately afterwards; it functions as a narrowly tailored derogation from the ordinary adversarial procedure. The norm sits at an operational, highly specific level, because it regulates only an urgent procedural scenario and does not set the general decision-making rule.

testo_originale: 3. The Commission shall base its decision only on grounds on which the undertakings concerned have been given the opportunity to submit their observations.
descrizione_funzionale: Guarantees the right to be heard by limiting the decision-maker to grounds that the undertakings have had a chance to comment on, thereby constraining the evidential and argumentative basis of the final act. It operates as a procedural safeguard at a fairly specific, operational level: not a general principle for the whole regime, but a targeted rule governing how one particular decision may be adopted.

testo_originale: 4. In order to be able to exercise its right pursuant to paragraph 1, the undertaking under investigation shall be entitled to have access to the file of the Commission. The right of access to the file shall not extend to confidential information or internal documents of the Commission or the Member States or, in particular, to correspondence between the Commission and the Member States. The right of access to the file shall be subject to the legitimate interest of undertakings or associations of undertakings in the protection of their business secrets and other confidential information. The Commission may ask the undertaking under investigation and the undertakings or associations of undertakings that provided information to the Commission to agree on terms to disclose that information. If the undertakings or associations of undertakings disagree on those terms, the Commission shall have the power to impose the terms on which the information is to be disclosed. Nothing in this paragraph shall prevent the Commission from using and disclosing, to the extent necessary, information that demonstrates the existence of a foreign subsidy distorting the internal market.
descrizione_funzionale: Procedural safeguard clause granting the investigated undertaking access to the case file while carving out protected categories of information, and it also equips the authority with a residual power to set disclosure terms where parties cannot agree. It operates at an intermediate, operational level: not a general principle, but a detailed rule governing how the adversarial process is balanced against confidentiality in a specific investigative setting.

testo_originale: Article 43 Professional secrecy and confidentiality
descrizione_funzionale: Protective rule imposing a duty of professional secrecy and confidentiality on those handling information under the regime, thereby safeguarding sensitive material and limiting disclosure in the course of enforcement. It operates at an intermediate-to-specific level: not a broad policy statement, but a cross-cutting operational safeguard that applies across the framework whenever confidential information is collected, used, or shared.

testo_originale: 1. Information acquired under this Regulation shall be used only for the purposes for which it was acquired, unless the provider of the information agrees otherwise.
descrizione_funzionale: This provision imposes a purpose-limitation rule on the handling of information, restricting its later use to the objective for which it was originally obtained unless consent for broader use is given. It operates as a targeted safeguard within the enforcement architecture, sitting at a fairly specific and technical level by governing a narrow aspect of information management rather than setting a general substantive standard.

testo_originale: 2. Member States and the Commission, their officials and other persons working under their supervision shall ensure the protection of confidential information acquired in application of this Regulation in accordance with the relevant applicable rules. To that end, they shall not disclose information covered by the obligation of professional secrecy that they have acquired pursuant to this Regulation.
descrizione_funzionale: Confidentiality and professional-secrecy clause imposing a duty on Member States, the Commission, and persons acting under their supervision to protect information obtained through the regulation, and prohibiting disclosure of covered material. It operates as an ancillary safeguard within the enforcement architecture, at a fairly specific and operational level, implementing a narrow protective rule rather than setting a general principle.

testo_originale: 3. Paragraphs 1 and 2 shall not prevent the publication of statistics and reports which do not contain information allowing the identification of specific undertakings or associations of undertakings.
descrizione_funzionale: Carves out a confidentiality limitation by clarifying that the preceding non-disclosure rule does not block the publication of aggregated statistics and reports, provided they cannot reveal the identity of particular entities. It operates at a fairly technical, implementation-focused level: a narrow exception that fine-tunes the broader secrecy regime without altering its core structure.

testo_originale: 4. The disclosure of any information communicated under this Regulation shall not prejudice the essential security interests of Member States.
descrizione_funzionale: Protective carve-out limiting the disclosure duty by preserving the ability of Member States to withhold information where publication would harm core security interests; it functions as a safeguard that qualifies the transparency regime rather than creating a new substantive obligation. The norm sits at a relatively specific, operational level, applying only to the handling of communicated information and introducing a narrow exception within the broader disclosure framework.

testo_originale: Article 44 Relationship to other instruments
descrizione_funzionale: Cross-reference clause that coordinates this act with the wider legal order by clarifying how it sits alongside other instruments and avoiding overlap or conflict. It operates at an intermediate, system-organising level: not a substantive rule in itself, but a structural provision that frames the act’s interaction with external norms.

testo_originale: 1. This Regulation is without prejudice to the application of Articles 101, 102, 106, 107 and 108 TFEU, Council Regulation (EC) No 1/2003 ( 23 ) and of Regulation (EC) No 139/2004.
descrizione_funzionale: Conflict-management and coordination clause preserving the continued operation of pre-existing competition and merger rules alongside this instrument, and cross-referencing them to avoid any implied displacement. It sits at a relatively high structural level: not a detailed operative rule, but a boundary-setting provision that situates the act within the wider legal order and clarifies how overlapping regimes interact.

testo_originale: 2. This Regulation is without prejudice to the application of Regulation (EU) 2016/1037 of the European Parliament and of the Council ( 24 ) .
descrizione_funzionale: Cross-reference clause preserving the continued application of another instrument and preventing any implied repeal or displacement by this Regulation. It operates at a structural, medium-low level of abstraction: not creating a new rule itself, but carving out the relationship between two regimes in a specific compatibility setting.

testo_originale: 3. This Regulation is without prejudice to the application of Regulation (EU) 2019/452.
descrizione_funzionale: Cross-reference clause preserving the separate operation of another legal regime and preventing any implied repeal or displacement by this act. It functions as a coordination rule at a fairly high structural level: not a substantive rule in itself, but a general safeguard that keeps the two frameworks legally distinct while allowing this Regulation to operate alongside the referenced one.

testo_originale: 4. This Regulation is without prejudice to the application of Regulation (EU) 2022/1031 of the European Parliament and of the Council ( 25 ) .
descrizione_funzionale: Cross-reference clause preserving the separate application of another instrument and preventing any implied repeal or conflict between the two regimes. It operates at a coordinating, system-level position: not creating new obligations itself, but delimiting the reach of this act by leaving an external rule-set intact.

testo_originale: 5. This Regulation takes precedence over Regulation (EU) 2016/1035 until that Regulation becomes applicable pursuant to its Article
descrizione_funzionale: Conflict-of-norms clause establishing the temporal priority of this act over another instrument until the latter itself becomes operative, thereby resolving overlap between two regulatory regimes. It sits at a fairly specific, transitional level: not a general principle of the framework, but a targeted rule governing how two texts interact during a limited period.

testo_originale: 18. Where, after that date, a foreign subsidy falls within the scope of application of both Regulation (EU) 2016/1035 and this Regulation, Regulation (EU) 2016/1035 takes precedence. However, the provisions applicable to public procurement and concentrations of this Regulation take precedence over Regulation (EU) 2016/1035.
descrizione_funzionale: Conflict-of-laws clause allocating priority between overlapping regulatory regimes, and carving out a specific override for the procurement and concentration rules in this act. The Commission may adopt such delegated acts to reduce the timelines in Article 25(2) and (4) and Article 30(2), (5) and (6) where its practice in the application of this Regulation demonstrates that the Commission’s assessment can be performed within a shorter period of time.
descrizione_funzionale: Delegating clause conferring a conditional power on the Commission to shorten specified review and investigation deadlines by means of delegated acts, subject to the procedural framework in the cited provision and to evidence from application practice that the assessments can be completed faster. It operates at an intermediate, structural level: not a broad principle, but a targeted adjustment mechanism that fine-tunes time limits in a defined set of procedures when experience shows the existing periods are longer than necessary.

testo_originale: Article 50 Exercise of the delegation
descrizione_funzionale: Delegation clause that authorises the Commission to adopt delegated acts and sets the institutional conditions for exercising that power, including the standard controls attached to such delegation. It operates at an intermediate, structural level: not a substantive rule for regulated parties, but a mechanism organising how the framework can be updated and refined over time.

testo_originale: 1. The power to adopt delegated acts is conferred on the Commission subject to the conditions laid down in this Article.
descrizione_funzionale: Empowerment clause granting the Commission authority to adopt delegated acts, while tying that authority to the safeguards and limits set out in the same article. It operates at an intermediate, structural level: not a substantive rule in itself, but a constitutional-style allocation of regulatory competence that frames how later detailed measures may be made.

testo_originale: 2. The power to adopt delegated acts referred to in Articles 49(1) and (5) shall be conferred on the Commission for a period of five years from 12 January
descrizione_funzionale: Delegation clause conferring on the Commission a time-limited authority to adopt supplementary acts under specified provisions, thereby enabling the framework to be updated through secondary rule-making. It sits at an intermediate, institutional level: more specific than the act’s general principles, but still structural rather than a narrow operational rule, because it organises who may act and for how long.

testo_originale: 3. The power to adopt delegated acts referred to in Article 49(9) shall be conferred on the Commission for a period of five years from 12 January
descrizione_funzionale: Delegation clause conferring a time-limited power on the Commission to adopt delegated acts under a specified enabling provision, thereby authorising supplementary rule-making within the framework. It sits at an intermediate, institutional level: more specific than the core substantive rules, but still structural because it organises how the framework can be completed and updated.

testo_originale: 2025. The Commission shall draw up a report in respect of the delegation of power not later than nine months before the end of the five-year period. The delegation of power shall be tacitly extended for periods of an identical duration, unless the European Parliament or the Council opposes such extension not later than three months before the end of each period.
descrizione_funzionale: Review-and-renewal clause governing the lifespan of the delegated rule-making authority: it requires the Commission to report on the delegation and sets the conditions under which that authority continues automatically unless either co-legislator objects. It sits at an intermediate, institutional level—more specific than the general empowerment itself, but still structural rather than a narrow operational rule.

testo_originale: 4. The delegation of power referred to in Article 49(1), (5) and (9) may be revoked at any time by the European Parliament or by the Council. A decision to revoke shall put an end to the delegation of the power specified in that decision. It shall take effect on the day following the publication of the decision in the Official Journal of the European Union or at a later date specified therein. It shall not affect the validity of any delegated acts already in force.
descrizione_funzionale: Revocation clause governing the political control of a delegated rule-making mandate, allowing either co-legislator to terminate the empowerment and preserving the legal effect of acts already adopted. It sits at an intermediate, institutional level: more specific than the general delegation itself, but still structural rather than a technical rule of application.

testo_originale: 5. Before adopting a delegated act, the Commission shall consult experts designated by each Member State in accordance with the principles laid down in the Interinstitutional Agreement of 13 April 2016 on Better Law-Making.
descrizione_funzionale: Consultation clause requiring the Commission to seek input from Member State-designated experts before exercising delegated rule-making authority, and tying that consultation to the principles of the Better Law-Making agreement. It operates at an intermediate, procedural level: not a substantive rule itself, but an institutional safeguard that conditions how a delegated power is prepared and exercised.

testo_originale: 6. As soon as it adopts a delegated act, the Commission shall notify it simultaneously to the European Parliament and to the Council.
descrizione_funzionale: Notification clause imposing an immediate institutional reporting duty once a delegated act is adopted, ensuring political oversight and transparency in the exercise of delegated rule-making power. It is a procedural, highly operational provision: narrow in scope and purely ancillary, implementing a specific step within the broader rule-making architecture rather than setting any substantive rule.

testo_originale: 7. A delegated act adopted pursuant to Article 49(1) (5) and (9) shall enter into force only if no objection has been expressed either by the European Parliament or by the Council within a period of two months of notification of that act to the European Parliament and the Council or if, before the expiry of that period, the European Parliament and the Council have both informed the Commission that they will not object. That period shall be extended by two months at the initiative of the European Parliament or of the Council.
descrizione_funzionale: Conditional entry-into-force clause for a delegated measure, establishing the scrutiny mechanism by which the measure becomes legally effective only absent objection from either co-legislator, with a built-in possibility of extending the review period. It operates at a highly operational level, supplying a precise procedural safeguard that governs a specific category of subordinate acts rather than laying down a general principle.

testo_originale: Article 51 Separate delegated acts for different delegated powers The Commission shall adopt a separate delegated act in respect of each power delegated to it pursuant to this Regulation.
descrizione_funzionale: This provision organises the exercise of delegated rule-making by requiring each delegated power under the act to be implemented through its own distinct delegated measure, rather than bundled together with others. It operates at an intermediate, structural level: not a broad principle of the regime, but a procedural coordination rule that governs how the delegated powers are formally used.

testo_originale: Article 52 Reporting and review
descrizione_funzionale: Review-and-accountability clause requiring the Commission to report on the application of the regime and to assess whether it should be revised. It operates at a high but not foundational level: it does not create substantive obligations for regulated parties, but instead provides an ongoing supervisory mechanism that can inform future adjustment of the framework.

testo_originale: 1. The Commission shall present an annual report on the application and implementation of this Regulation to the European Parliament and to the Council.
descrizione_funzionale: Reporting obligation requiring the Commission to account periodically to the political institutions for how the regime is being applied and carried out. It operates at an intermediate level: not a substantive rule governing conduct, but an oversight mechanism that supports transparency, monitoring, and institutional control across the whole framework.

testo_originale: 2. By 13 July 2026 and every three years thereafter, the Commission shall review its practice of implementing and enforcing this Regulation, in particular with regard to the application of Articles 4, 5, 6 and 9, and the notification thresholds set out in Article 20(3), Article 28(1) and (2), and present a report to the European Parliament and the Council, accompanied, where the Commission considers it appropriate, by relevant legislative proposals. In the context of its review, the Commission shall report on developments in international relations regarding third countries’ subsidy control systems.
descrizione_funzionale: Periodic review and reporting clause that obliges the Commission to assess how the regime is being applied and enforced, with a possible follow-up of legislative proposals. It operates at an intermediate-to-high level of abstraction: not a technical rule for individual cases, but a supervisory mechanism that periodically recalibrates the whole framework and its key trigger points.

testo_originale: 3. Where the Commission considers it appropriate to combine the report with relevant legislative proposals, such proposals may include:
descrizione_funzionale: Discretionary coordination clause allowing the Commission to attach legislative proposals to a report when it deems that useful, thereby linking review output to possible follow-up norm-setting. It operates at an intermediate, institutional level: not a broad principle, but a procedural gateway that opens a further legislative track in a specific case.

testo_originale: (a) amending the thresholds for notifications as set out in Articles 20 and 28;
descrizione_funzionale: Technical amendment clause adjusting the notification thresholds referenced in two operative provisions, thereby recalibrating when the reporting obligation is triggered. It sits at a narrow, implementation-focused level, modifying a specific quantitative parameter within the existing framework rather than setting any general rule.

testo_originale: (b) exempting certain categories of undertakings concerned from the obligation to notify pursuant to Articles 21 and 29, especially where the practice of the Commission enables the identification of economic activities where foreign subsidies are unlikely to distort the internal market;
descrizione_funzionale: Delegating clause authorising the Commission to exempt defined categories of undertakings from the notification duty under the cited provisions, while tying that discretion to established administrative practice and an assessment of low distortion risk. It operates at an intermediate, implementation-oriented level: not a general principle, but a targeted rule that fine-tunes when the core reporting mechanism applies.

testo_originale: (c) establishing specific thresholds for notifications for certain economic sectors or differentiated thresholds for different types of public procurement contracts, especially where the practice of the Commission enables the identification of economic activities where foreign subsidies are more likely to distort the internal market, including as regards strategic sectors and critical infrastructure;
descrizione_funzionale: Delegated rule-making clause authorising the Commission to set sector-specific or contract-specific notification thresholds, thereby fine-tuning when a filing obligation is triggered in particular market contexts. It operates at an intermediate, operational level: more specific than the general framework, but still flexible and technical, aimed at calibrating the regime to identifiable risk patterns rather than laying down a universal rule.

testo_originale: (d) amending the timelines for review and in-depth investigations as set out in Articles 25 and 30;
descrizione_funzionale: Operative cross-referencing clause that adjusts the procedural timetable for review and in-depth examination by modifying the deadlines already laid down elsewhere in the act. It sits at a fairly technical, implementation-focused level, fine-tuning how the existing decision-making machinery works in a specific procedural context rather than setting any general principle.

testo_originale: (e) abrogating this Regulation, if the Commission considers that multilateral rules to address foreign subsidies distorting the internal market have rendered this Regulation fully redundant.
descrizione_funzionale: Termination clause conferring a discretionary power on the Commission to repeal the act once a specified external regulatory development makes the framework unnecessary. It operates at a high but not foundational level: a system-closing safeguard that applies to the whole instrument, yet only in the exceptional case where a broader multilateral regime has fully displaced the need for the regulation.

testo_originale: Article 53 Transitional provisions
descrizione_funzionale: Transitional clause governing the shift from the old regime to the new one by preserving legal continuity for situations already underway and preventing gaps or retroactive disruption. It operates at a practical, system-management level: not a broad substantive rule, but a targeted bridging provision that applies only to the changeover period.

testo_originale: 1. This Regulation shall apply to foreign subsidies granted in the five years prior to 12 July 2023 where such foreign subsidies distort the internal market after 12 July
descrizione_funzionale: Transitional applicability clause that extends the Regulation’s reach backward in time for a defined pre-entry period, thereby determining which earlier measures can still trigger the new regime. It operates at a fairly specific, implementation-oriented level: not a general principle, but a temporal rule that calibrates the framework’s scope in a narrow and technical way.

testo_originale: 2. By way of derogation to paragraph 1, this Regulation shall apply to foreign financial contributions granted in the three years prior to 12 July 2023 where such foreign financial contributions were granted to an undertaking notifying a concentration or notifying financial contributions in the context of a public procurement procedure pursuant to this Regulation.
descrizione_funzionale: Derogation clause extending the temporal reach of the regime to certain pre-cutoff contributions, but only for undertakings involved in a notified concentration or a notified procurement-related procedure. It operates at a highly specific, transitional level, carving out a narrow exception to the general temporal rule rather than laying down a broad principle.

testo_originale: 3. This Regulation shall not apply to concentrations for which the agreement was concluded, the public bid was announced, or a controlling interest was acquired before 12 July
descrizione_funzionale: Transitional exclusion clause carving out a defined category of transactions from the Regulation’s reach by reference to a pre-existing temporal event, thereby limiting the scope of application. It operates at a highly specific, technical level: not a general principle, but a narrow cut-off rule that determines when the framework does not attach.

testo_originale: 4. This Regulation shall not apply to public procurement contracts that have been awarded or procedures initiated before 12 July 2023.
descrizione_funzionale: Transitional exclusion clause carving out pre-existing procurement situations from the regulation’s reach, thereby limiting its temporal application and preventing retroactive effect. It operates at a highly specific, implementation-focused level, as a narrow exception that only affects a defined set of cases already underway before a fixed date.

testo_originale: Article 54 Entry into force and date of application 1. This Regulation shall enter into force on the twentieth day following that of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union . 2. It shall apply from 12 July 2023. 3. By way of derogation from paragraph 2 of this Article, Articles 47 and 48 shall apply from 11 January 2023 and Article 14(5), (6) and (7) shall apply from 12 January 2024. 4. By way of derogation from paragraph 2 of this Article, Articles 21 and 29 shall apply from 12 October 2023.
descrizione_funzionale: Commencement and application clause that fixes when the act becomes legally effective and staggers the start of particular provisions through specific derogations, thereby coordinating the temporal operation of the whole framework. It sits at a very high level of abstraction for the instrument as a whole, but the staggered dates introduce narrow implementation details for selected rules rather than any substantive standard.

testo_originale: Article 1 The transitional period concerning the acquisition of agricultural land in Croatia referred to in Chapter 3 of Annex V to the 2011 Act of Accession shall be extended until 30 June 2023.
descrizione_funzionale: Operative extension clause that prolongs the duration of an existing derogation by fixing a new end date, thereby keeping the special regime in force for a further period. It sits at a narrow, implementation-focused level: it does not create the underlying regime, but adjusts one temporal parameter of its application within the broader accession framework.

testo_originale: Article 2 This Decision shall enter into force on the day of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union .
descrizione_funzionale: Commencement clause that determines when the decision becomes legally effective by tying its operation to publication in the Official Journal. It is a highly specific, purely procedural rule at the lowest end of the abstraction spectrum, applying automatically to the whole instrument without adding any substantive content.

testo_originale: Article 1 Annex I to Regulation (EC) No 184/2005 is amended in accordance with the Annex to this Regulation.
descrizione_funzionale: Amendment clause that directly modifies an existing annex by incorporating the changes set out in the attached schedule, thereby updating the operative content of the parent act without creating a standalone rule. It sits at a highly specific, technical level, functioning as an implementation mechanism for a narrow textual revision rather than laying down any general principle.

testo_originale: Article 2 This Regulation shall enter into force on the day following that of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union . It shall apply from the day following that on which the United Kingdom ceases to be a Member State of the Union.
descrizione_funzionale: Commencement and application clause fixing when the act becomes legally operative and when its practical effect is triggered by a future external event. It operates at a procedural, system-wide level: universal in reach for the instrument as a whole, but purely temporal and implementation-oriented rather than substantive.
